Class ResourceShareService

java.lang.Object
cloudpage.service.ResourceShareService

    • leave

      public void leave(String recipientId, String shareId)
      Lets a recipient drop a share that was given to them. Only removes their own access; the owner's data is untouched. Distinct from revoke(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), which is the owner withdrawing access.

      public void uploadToShare(String shareId, User recipient, String folderPath, org.springframework.web.multipart.MultipartFile file) throws IOException
      Adds a new file to a folder share. Requires EDIT. The file lands in the owner's storage and counts against the owner's quota, so collaborators cannot fill their own space with someone else's shared folder.

    • deleteInShare

      public void deleteInShare(String shareId, User recipient, String childPath) throws IOException
      Deletes a file or folder inside a share. Requires EDIT.

      Files are moved into the owner's trash, exactly as if the owner had deleted the file themselves — a recipient with EDIT access must not be able to destroy the owner's data with no recovery path. See the class-level note on folders below.

      Folders are still hard-deleted here, matching FolderController's own delete endpoint for the owner's own folders: this codebase has no folder-level trash mechanism at all today (TrashService.moveToTrash(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.String) only accepts a single regular file). Routing folder deletes through trash is real follow-up work — it needs a trash design that can hold a whole subtree, restore it, and account for its size against retention/quota — not a one-line change here, so it is intentionally out of scope for this fix rather than silently expanding it.

      Throws:
      IOException
